questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Charcot's triad of multiple sclerosis consists of:
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Multiple Sclerosis (PDF p. 430)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug is the medication of choice for spasticity in multiple sclerosis?
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, MS Management (PDF p. 430)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which teaching is appropriate for a client with multiple sclerosis?
questions.rationale: Heat worsens symptoms and sensory loss risks burns; avoid strenuous exercise.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, MS Nursing (PDF p. 431)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Weakness beginning in the legs and ascending after a viral illness suggests:
questions.rationale: GBS: ascending weakness and diminished reflexes from peripheral demyelination.
questions.quote: Diminished reflexes and muscle weakness that goes upward

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the priority assessment for a client with Guillain-Barré syndrome?
questions.rationale: Ascending paralysis can affect the diaphragm; monitor ventilation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GBS Nursing (PDF p. 431)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Parkinson's disease is associated with decreased:
questions.rationale: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Parkinson's Disease (PDF p. 432)
questions.quote: Associated with decreased levels of dopamine

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding is characteristic of Parkinson's disease?
questions.rationale: Resting pill-rolling tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, mask-like face, festinating gait.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Parkinson's Manifestations (PDF p. 432)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Very small, illegible handwriting in Parkinson's disease is called:
questions.rationale: Micrographia results from bradykinesia and rigidity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Parkinson's Manifestations (PDF p. 432)
questions.quote: Micrographia (very minute and often illegible handwriting)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which vitamin reduces the effect of levodopa (without carbidopa)?
questions.rationale: Pyridoxine, phenothiazines, and reserpine block levodopa.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Levodopa Teaching (PDF p. 433)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client starting levodopa should be taught to rise slowly because of:
questions.rationale: Levodopa side effects include orthostatic hypotension, nausea, confusion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Levodopa Side Effects (PDF p. 433)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet helps a client with Parkinson's disease who has dysphagia?
questions.rationale: Semi-solids and thick fluids reduce aspiration.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Parkinson's Nursing (PDF p. 433)
questions.quote: Provide semi-solid diet and thick fluids

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Riluzole is used in ALS because it:
questions.rationale: ALS involves glutamate over-excitation; riluzole is a glutamate antagonist.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Spontaneous twitching of muscles seen in ALS is called:

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.rationale: High cervical injury impairs the diaphragm; airway is first priority.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Spinal Cord Injury (PDF p. 435)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: At an accident scene with suspected spinal injury, the nurse should:
options: Immobilize and move as a unit
questions.rationale: Immobilize on a firm surface with collar; do not realign; log-roll.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, SCI Management (PDF p. 435)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with T4 injury suddenly has pounding headache, sweating, and very high BP. This is:
questions.rationale: Autonomic dysreflexia occurs with injuries above T6.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Dysreflexia (PDF p. 436)
questions.quote: Life threatening complication that occurs in patients with injuries above the T6 level.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the first nursing action in autonomic dysreflexia?
questions.rationale: Sit upright to lower BP, then find the cause (usually a full bladder).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Dysreflexia (PDF p. 436)
questions.quote: Position the patient in sitting position to decrease BP

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The most common trigger of autonomic dysreflexia is:
questions.rationale: Bladder distention; also fecal impaction and pressure ulcers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Dysreflexia (PDF p. 436)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which brain changes are found in Alzheimer's disease?
questions.rationale: Amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, and cortical atrophy.
questions.quote: Development of amyloid-containing neuritic plaques & neurofibrillary tangles
